title: Top-account rapid commitment thresholds and scope scarcity matrix
creator: Ava Ramirez
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable gating mechanism (Commitment Velocity Thresholds) plus a Scope Scarcity Matrix to decide rapid commitments for top accounts that request roadmap changes or escalations. Deliverables: 1) threshold rulesheet to convert signals (ARR, renewal proximity, severity) to a commitment band, 2) a scope scarcity matrix to trade off feature scope vs delivery runway for promise windows, 3) an intake response template and SLA table for initial customer-facing replies.
problem_statement: We receive frequent inbound escalation requests from strategic accounts that are time-sensitive. Current intake relies on ad hoc judgement and causes inconsistent commitments and downstream sprint churn. This leads to engineering context switching and potential SLA misses for other customers.
goals: Reduce time-to-initial-commit (first internal decision) for top-account escalations to under 72 hours
Provide a repeatable rubric that maps account signals to commitment bands (No, Explore, Timeboxed, Committed)
Minimize scope creep by introducing a scarcity matrix that preserves delivery runway for existing roadmap OKRs
success_metrics: Median internal decision time for top-account escalations <= 72 hours
<= 15% increase in sprint rework attributable to accepted top-account asks during pilot quarter
NPS feedback from 10 pilot accounts on clarity of commitment > 4.0
proposed_solution: Define Commitment Velocity Thresholds: numeric scoring of signals (ARR weight, renewal_in_30d, incident_count_90d, strategic_planned_deal_stage)
Create Scope Scarcity Matrix: axis of scope size (tiny/small/medium/large) vs runway risk (low/medium/high) with default mitigation actions
Design intake form with mandatory fields mapped to threshold scoring and auto-generated commitment band
Pilot with three high-touch accounts for one cycle, measure outcomes and adjust weights
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize scoring weights with Sales/CS/Engineering review (doc + workshop)
Week 2: Implement intake form and automated scoring in Zendesk + internal Confluence sheet
Week 3: Run pilot with 3 accounts; update internal playbook and update Console escalation links
Week 4: Evaluate pilot metrics and present decision to GTM/Eng leadership for wider rollout
risks: Over-weighting revenue signals could bias roadmap away from high-impact but low-revenue features
Engineering may resist timeboxed commitments if policy does not account for existing capacity constraints
Customers may perceive the matrix as bureaucratic if communication templates are not customer-friendly
open_questions: Should renewals within 60 days carry a multiplier vs 30 days?
What is the cutoff ARR for automatic promotion into higher commitment bands?
Which telemetry source will be the canonical incident count for scoring (PagerDuty vs Console alerts)?
acceptance_criteria: Thresholds documented and agreed by Sales/CS/Eng in PRD
Intake form implemented and scoring validated with two historical cases
Pilot executed with 3 accounts and initial metrics captured in dashboard
Playbook and customer-facing templates approved by Legal
